Hi,
Playtested and went deep into the referee, the statement, and the three bosses while writing a bot for it. It's a solid, well-built game! :) 
The rock-paper-scissors design is geometrically fair (the three camps are pairwise equidistant in manhattan distance, obstacles are 4-fold symmetric), the capture-then-release ordering is handled correctly, and the referee code is clean and readable. 

A few suggestions that I think would maybe improve it:

- Low leagues feel very swingy. Since the game ends the instant one tribe is fully captured, the 1–2 unit leagues often resolve in 2–6 turns, decided mostly by spawn geometry and who collides first. For a ladder that's a lot of variance --> in the 1-unit league you might play a fixed number of turns and rank by captures, or use best-of-N.

- Eliminated players rank last even if they captured the most. So a player who scored 2–3 then got fully imprisoned finishes behind someone on 0. 
If that isn't intended, keep their capture count for ranking, otherwise it's worth stating explicitly that survival beats scoring.

- Lots of 0–0 stalemate draws in League 3. On the larger maps, equal move speed makes a competent elemental nearly impossible to catch without cornering. I see many 200-turn 0–0 games, even boss vs boss. --> Smaller maps for the unit counts, more choke-point obstacles, or an aggression incentive would help. 

- The highest-leverage idea: make units block movement (right now everyone phases through everyone), that alone adds body-blocking/cornering and would cut the stalemates significantly.

A couple of harsh, undocumented "instant loss" edges:
- An empty or malformed MSG (e.g. MSG with no text) matches no pattern --> deactivates the player --> loss, 
- Exceeding the hidden unitsPerPlayer * 3 command cap --> "Too many commands" --> loss. 
Neither is in the statement. I'd ignore an empty MSG instead of killing the player, and document the command limit.

Boss progression: The random --> greedy --> risk-map curve is good! 

Nice work overall! Upvoted! :)

Comment: This project deserves approval because it offers much more than a simple pathfinding challenge. Players must balance offense and defense, predict opponents' movements, and take advantage of the rock-paper-scissors relationship between the three elemental tribes. The simultaneous capture system creates interesting strategic situations where positioning and timing are critical. The game is easy to understand thanks to its simple rules, yet it provides significant depth for AI development. Participants can explore pathfinding, target prioritization, threat assessment, territory control, and opponent prediction. The presence of three players instead of two also makes the gameplay less predictable and encourages more diverse strategies.
Could this be the new Codingame Challenge? looks pretty well designed, and really nice.

It could use some UI like avatars in square at the side or top so one could know who's who by game screenshot. Also something like MSG a short message, either per elemental, or one next to avatar would be also good.

Simultaneous moves and the possibility of swapping positions with the opponent make captures impossible without luck, dedicating 4+ elementals to the capture, or someone entering a dead-end path while being next to 2+ predators. On top of that, 3+ player free-for-all games are particularly hard to design, and I'm not sure I see too much strategic depth here that doesn't boil down to guessing opponents' moves correctly, even if luck-based captures weren't a problem.

I suggest adding tooltips with coordinates to each cell. Right now you give the position for each elemental, but the rest has to be done by counting.

When you MOVE the same unit id twice, you lose the game. On CodinGame it's common to give a warning and ignore the action, as long as it's syntactically correct.

For a perfectly symmetric map you would need a hexagon grid. Not saying that you should do that, it would make catching too hard I think.

Order of explanation
* The overall readability would benefit from reordering the sections for a more logical flow of mechanics: Actions => Movement => Captures => Prisoners.

* Reordering would also allow you to remove some redundancy, particularly the first paragraph in the current Movement section.

Actions
* Please format "x" and "y" in "(x, y)" using <var> tags. You may keep parentheses/comma unformatted or continue to wrap them in <const> if preferred.

Movements
* Please clarify whether movement is:
  - 4-directional (N, S, E, W), or
  - 8-directional (including diagonals).

* Please specify a deterministic rule (e.g. fixed direction priority order) when multiple shortest paths exist.

Capture
* Please specify whether anything happens when prey enters an enemy camp.

Game End
* "At least one player has all their elementals prisoner.": Needs a wording fix. Suggested rewrite:

At least one player has all of their elementals captured as prisoners.

Technical Details
* "The score of a team is the number of prisoners belonging to its prey team.": Sounds slightly awkward. Suggested rewrite:

The score of a team is the number of prisoners it has captured.

Inputs
* Please state in the following values are integers in the relevant descriptions:
  - mapSize
  - elementsCount
  - elementalId
  - x
  - y

Inputs / Default stub
* Please change "prisoner" from bool to int, as some language stubs don't provide a bool to the player (e.g. Lua, Pascal). Use 0 / 1 instead of false / true.

Output
* Please format "x" and "y" in "(x, y)" using <var> tags. You may keep parentheses/comma unformatted or continue to wrap them in <const> if preferred.

Constraints
* Consider clarifying camp distribution:
  - Does each player always have exactly one camp?
  - Is the number of camps and elementals guaranteed to be equal for all players?

Leagues
* Do you plan to introduce additional mechanics in later leagues? For example, the story mentions rescuing elementals; will that be implemented?

Referee / Viewer
* I'll perform some testing later.

Thanks.

Hi everyone,

I've just published a Work In Progress version of my multiplayer game Elemental Wars.
It's a 3-player tactical game based on a rock-paper-scissors dynamic (Water / Fire / Plant), with simultaneous captures and simple pathfinding-based movement.

At this stage, the core mechanics are in place:
- movement toward a target (1 step per turn),
- simultaneous captures,
- prisoners system,
- (later leagues) release mechanics.

I'm mainly looking for feedback on:
- clarity of the rules / statement,
- gameplay feel and balance,
- edge cases or unclear situations,
- overall fun factor

Don't hesitate to try it out and share your thoughts even early impressions are very helpful!
Thanks

Cumulative scoring, "highest score wins," releases not subtracting points, and a fully imprisoned tribe ending the game but being ranked on its captures (not auto-last) are all consistent between the referee and the statement text.
